citations.quote: that VALUE clause applies and any VALUE clause specified in the description of type-name-1 is ignored for this entry

cases.reason: The pointer is the wrong rule: 2002 GR3 is the VALUE rule; its words were swapped with BASED by the similarity match. The 2023 VALUE rule (GR3) says something else ("the content of the literal ... is used for the initial value", plus implicit-PICTURE inheritance) and does not state that the type-name VALUE is ignored. Neither 2023 row shows the 2002 override-and-ignore behaviour; l1c34_type_subject_based (BASED) passes at 2002 but is about BASED. Probe shows the compiler correct at 2002, including a CD record.
cases.needs: its own verdict: the compiler at --std 2002 applies the subject VALUE and ignores the type-name VALUE (probes p01-type-value-ws/-cd); a 2002 witness from those probes

cases.reason: 2002 13.16.59 (USING clause) has one format, USING identifier-1, and its intro confines it to ACCEPT screen / DISPLAY screen; no CD, report or debugging reach. SR3 lists the sections identifier-1 may be in (communication section excluded, so no CD reach). The whole screen section is processor-dependent in 2002 (B.3 item 1), and 3.1.5 lets an implementation not support it given a compile-time warning; the pinned compiler refuses screen USING at --std 2002 with COBOL1560 (reader's probe and mine), same as the 2023 DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT row. 2023 adds a variable-length-group prohibition (narrower), irrelevant under non-support. Minor: the COBOL1560 text at --std 2002 cites the 2023 optional-module licence (§2023:4.2.7, A.4.2) rather than 2002's processor-dependent licence (B.3); diagnostic wording, not the requirement.
